extracted.intended_audience: community organizations and small businesses (Polk County residents) seeking grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, local-government guidance on how to research grant opportunities online and prepare applications for community groups and small businesses, including finding suitable funders, checking eligibility, budgeting parts of a project, and assembling required documents before deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use online research and search engines
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you have your project in place, researching for grants can primarily be done online. Make use of your favorite internet search engine and define key words and phrases in your grant research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate clear keywords and phrases related to your project when searching; use search engines and grant databases to find opportunities. Repeat searches regularly to capture new or updated opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and use appropriate keywords/phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Define key words and phrases in your grant research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about terms that describe your project, population served, activities, and location to narrow search results to relevant funders and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check geographic eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: In your research, look for specific geographical limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that the funder accepts applications from your city/county/state or targets your geographic area before investing time in application preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate funding needs by project component
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for how much money each part of your project may need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break the project into components and estimate costs for each so you can determine whether a grant's award size matches your needs and tailor budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor websites frequently for updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you do your web searches often as many websites are updated daily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-check funder sites and listings regularly for changes in deadlines, requirements, or newly posted opportunities; set calendar reminders or RSS/email alerts if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track deadlines and required submission documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When researching a grant pay attention to application deadlines and documents required upon submittal of your grant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile a checklist of required materials (e.g., applications, budgets, attachments) and their deadlines so you can schedule work and gather materials in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain third-party documents and letters early
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grant deadline is in the next few days and you are required to submit documents from your CPA or letters of recommendation showing how your project has impacted the community, you may be cutting it too close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request CPA documents, partnership letters, and recommendation letters well before the deadline; avoid last-minute dependence on third parties that can delay submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review past awardees to assess fit with funder priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Look to see if the grantor’s website will allow you to see past awardees so you can determine if you meet their requirements based on what the grantee is looking for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study previous recipients to understand the types of projects funded, typical award amounts, and whether your project aligns with the funder's priorities and selection patterns.
